minutes.headline: Sewer Commission chose MP for pump station maintenance over lower-rate Watermark; vote count unclear, quorum then lost.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed two bids for pump station operation and maintenance. Jack reported on reference checks and recommended the incumbent interim vendor, MP. After discussion, a motion to accept MP's contract, amended to one year or through the fiscal year, was voted. Members then left, quorum was lost, and public comment was cut short.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether it was a hearing; urged watching the contract closely, not putting all eggs in one basket, and a side-by-side cost comparison of prior vendor expenses and MP's proposal.
Mr. Luck, as a resident, said the meeting had no quorum and public comment should have come at the beginning.

votes.motion: Informal poll on hiring Watermark, going around the board
Motion to accept MP's contract, amended to one year or through the end of the fiscal year as the procurement manager recommends

budget_items.topic: Pump station O&M RFP base contract
budget_items.what_was_said: The two bids were within a couple hundred dollars on the base contract, a virtual tie.
Watermark's hourly rates were far lower than MP's, but Watermark's would not apply to subcontracted repairs.

budget_items.topic: Interim MP rate vs new proposed rate
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled the interim contract paying MP a lower hourly rate than the new proposal.
A member said MP's rates are far higher than Watermark's, worse in overtime, and that MP's quote assumes only 10 hours a week.
Extra hours at MP's rates would add up, and third-party cleaning and jetting would be extra for either vendor.
Members said the prior vendor ran well over budget as emergencies rose.

decisions.decision: Contract term to be set as one year or through end of the fiscal year, as the procurement manager recommends; town manager and counsel to review the contract.
The contract goes to Barb and the town manager; the temporary contract runs to mid-September.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission moved to accept MP's contract for pump station operation and maintenance, amended to one year or through the fiscal year; the vote count was not audible.
The contract term was set at one year or through the end of the fiscal year, with the town manager and counsel to review the contract.
The contract goes to Barb and the town manager; the temporary contract runs to mid-September.
Members heard the two bids were nearly tied on the base contract, while Watermark's hourly rates were far lower than MP's and would not cover subcontracted repairs.
Members left after the vote, quorum was lost, and public comment was cut short; a resident said comment should have come at the start.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates pay for pump station upkeep, and the choice of vendor sets hourly and overtime costs that can rise beyond the base contract if repairs or emergencies grow.
Because the vote count is not audible and quorum was lost afterward, residents may want to confirm from the official record that the selection was validly taken.
watch_next: Review of the MP contract by the town manager and counsel, before the temporary contract runs out in mid-September.
